Hoarding limit on photo · 2. Plan and elevation · 3. Melamine layout · 4. Suggested Build Sequence · 5. Site checks · 6. Materials form 1. Hoarding limit on the photo Gus's markup on the site photo: the blue outline is the hoarding limit on the floor and the crossed box is the entry. The green boxes show the old fixing marks where tracks were used before, beside the fire door.
2. Plan and elevation All sizes in mm. The dashed red line is the lease line (the shopfront): nothing is fixed to it.

3. Melamine layout and cutting plan Each panel is numbered by the sheet it is cut from. Full sheets S1 to S7 go in whole; the cut pieces sit at the corners. S8 gives the 1100 strip for the front left. S9 gives the 600 strip for the left return and the 400 strip for the right return. S10 is turned sideways and cut to one 1600 x 1200 piece above the entry. Note: instead of cutting S10, the door-top pieces can be cut in the factory from a spare sheet and sent to the job. Each top is the same width as the sheet below it, so every join is one straight line from floor to top. Tops T1 to T7 go in whole. T8 is cut 1100. T9 is cut 600 + 400. Above the entry goes one 1600 x 600 piece cut from S10.

4. Suggested Build Sequence Build left to right as seen from the mall: left return (track section first), front, right return. 1 Check the truck. Before leaving, check the truck against the materials form to make sure all the material was loaded, including the 2 spare sheets. 2 Arrive and secure the area. Sign in with centre management. Set up barrier tape and the bollard around the work zone. Lay the dust suppression. 3 Set out the hoarding limit. From the fire door wall, mark the left return 3000 long, 300 left of the shop's side wall. Snap the 7500 front line parallel to the shopfront, 1600 out from the lease line. The right return runs 1600 back to the lease line. 4 Mark the entry. Measure 4700 from the left corner along the front line and mark a 1600 opening (4700 to 6300); it ends 1200 from the right end. 5 Fix the tracks and timbers. Along the first 1400 of the left return from the fire door wall, fix 90 mm track to the ceiling and to the floor. Stand 3 x 90x45 MGP10 timbers (4.2 m) in the tracks at 600 centres; the melamine is screwed to them. Suggestion only: BSG is still learning this method. 6 Stand the Titan uprights. 7 uprights with 6 counterweights each (weight matrix for 4.2 m), each one at a joint between two sheets, never in the middle of a sheet, and none in the corners (no room there): left return at 2400 from the fire door wall; front at 1100, 2300, 3500, 4700, 6300 from the left corner; right return at 400 from the front corner. They are marked on the melamine layout. Plus 1 spare upright (10%), not placed on the layout, with its 6 counterweights. 48 counterweights are sent (8 x 6). 7 Frame the walls. Fix the 70 x 45 MGP 10 studs (4.2 m) so every melamine joint lands on a stud. Frame the entry with 2 x 4.2 m and 4 x 2.3 m door studs and a head at 2400. 8 Fix the 3600 sheets. Left return S1, S2, S9a (600, at the corner); front left S3, S4, S5, S8 (1100, at the corner); front right S6; right return S7, S9b (400, at the corner). 9 Fill above the entry. One 1600 x 1200 piece (S10) between the door head at 2400 and 3600. 10 Fix the tops. 600 tops from 3600 to 4200 along the whole run. Each top is the same width as the sheet below it, so every join is one straight line from floor to top. Tops T1 to T7 go in whole. T8 is cut 1100. T9 is cut 600 + 400. Above the entry goes one 1600 x 600 piece cut from S10. 11 Hang the doors. Two 2340 leaves on 4 hinges, metal plates and deadbolt. Check they close and lock. 12 Finish. White tape on every vertical joint, black skirting tape along the base, screw covers, anti-tampers, 6 warning stickers, paint touch-ups. 13 Hand over. Clean up, remove the barrier, photograph each side, complete the installation certificate and sign INST CHK. 5. Site checks Confirm before fixing anything; update the drawings if any differ. [ ] The front measures 7500 and runs parallel to the shopfront. [ ] The ceiling is at 4200 along the run and is sound for fixing the track beside the fire door (the old fixing marks show where it went before). [ ] The entry starts 4700 from the left corner (1200 from the right end). [ ] The 1600 right return leaves the walkway centre management requires. [ ] Nothing is fixed to the shopfront; outside the track section the Titan counterweights hold the hoarding. 6. Materials form follows on the next page.

How this price is worked out  Pacific Fair hoardings are charged per lineal metre (lm) under the agreed BSG Commercial Internal Hoarding Schedule of Rates for GPT - Pacific Fair 25-26.  The lineal metres are the full hoarding run, which includes the returns and sides as well as the front: 3,000 + 7,500 + 1,600 = 12,100 mm = 12.1 lm.  The hoarding is 4,200 mm high, so it falls in the up to 4.2 m high band at $320.00 per lm (ex GST). The rate rises with height because taller hoardings need more melamine, more counterweights per upright and more labour to install safely.  The run is above the 10 lm minimum charge, so the actual length is charged.  12.1 lm x $320.00 = $3,872.00 ex GST, plus GST at 10%. 4. What is included  Supply, delivery, installation and removal of the TITAN free-standing hoarding system.  Structural engineering certification to AS4687 (pre-engineered certified hoarding).  16 mm white melamine boards with white taped joints and black skirting tape along the bottom.  One set of double doors, opening 2340 mm high x 1600 mm wide, with barrel bolt (deadbolt lock provided by Pacific Fair).  Free-standing installation: nothing is fixed to the centre's finishes, so there is no damage and no make-good work when the hoarding is removed.  Hoarding drawing for approval (attached).  Hoarding on site for up to 6 months before further charges apply.
